  "markdown_report": "**Proposed direction: candidate-competition auditing for the existing HSTU.** At 0% progress, prioritize reproducible diagnostics before training changes.

**Starting insights.** (1) Training margins average 9.64–10.94, with negative-win rates below 0.2%; validation ranking remains unmeasured. (2) Final-event deletion reduces margins by 3.10–4.06, while prefix-shuffle mean changes are at most 0.01. Deletion changes readout and coordinates, so this does not establish shortcut learning. (3) Qualitative feedback distinguishes relatedness from usefulness; titles/descriptions cannot establish ownership, fulfilled needs, or undocumented compatibility.

**Related-work insights.** (1) Sampled metrics can reverse comparisons; repeated draws estimate variance without removing sampling bias [1,2]. Candidate panels remain stress tests. (2) CATS and earlier negative-mining work identify the hard-negative/false-negative trade-off [3,4]; similar unobserved items remain uncertain competitors. (3) Product taxonomies distinguish incompatibility from insufficient evidence [5].

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Existing evidence | Next measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Competition | Strong training-pair separation | Fixed panels with frequency controls |
| History | Endpoint-dominated sensitivity | Candidate-specific prefix sensitivity |
| Evidence | Broad relevance, uncertain usefulness | Specification evidence coverage |

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fixed competition panels** [1–4,6] | 4/6/5 | Originality: useful HSTU integration; potential: isolates diagnostic gaps; difficulty: reuses scoring hooks | Originality: established methods; potential: training ranks may reflect memorization; difficulty: matched sampling and reproducibility require care |
| Prefix-only item dropout | 3/5/4 | Originality: targeted ablation; potential: tests robustness; difficulty: retains backbone | Originality: standard augmentation; potential: may remove useful context without reducing endpoint dependence; difficulty: retraining required |
| Evidence-backed specification audit [5] | 5/6/6 | Originality: connects evidence to ranking; potential: distinguishes unknowns; difficulty: needs no pretrained weights | Originality: established taxonomy; potential: sparse evidence; difficulty: normalization needs auditing |

**Selected algorithm.** Retain the original uniform, positive-frequency-bin, and lexical panels; add a control matching the lexical panel’s training-frequency-bin histogram. The lexical/control contrast reduces binned-frequency confounding, although within-bin frequency and other attributes remain uncontrolled. Each panel contains 99 unique row-unobserved competitors, preserving the original positive and history exclusions.

Freeze vocabulary, IDF, cleaning, item ordering, parameters, package versions, and seed-42-derived sampling plans. Retrieve positive-similarity lexical neighbors in bounded catalog blocks; resolve ties before truncation. Report zero-text rows, eligible-neighbor counts, coverage, excluded-query characteristics, ranks, margins, ties, and panel overlap. Compare all panels on common eligible queries, with pair-specific coverage additionally reported. Repeat stochastic panels five times; report draw variation descriptively without treating repeats as users.

Training-history selection and lexical coverage can favor memorized, popular, or well-described targets. These measurements cannot establish generalization, usefulness, causal preferences, or expected uplift. Preserve identity controls, final-nonpadding readout, diagnostic interfaces, four routes, and one unchanged HSTU checkpoint/category. Only pinned macro validation HR@10 selects subsequent training changes.",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Extend the deterministic HSTU candidate-competition audit with explicit frequency controls, reproducible lexical retrieval, coverage accounting, and prespecified candidate-draw repetitions. Retain uniform, positive-frequency-bin, and lexical-neighbor panels, and add a fourth panel matching the lexical panel's training-frequency-bin histogram. Each category retains its existing single trained HSTU model, checkpoint, predictor, and host evaluator.",
    "motivation": "Strong separation from supplied training negatives does not establish strong ranking against plausible competitors. The original lexical-versus-uniform comparison also confounds lexical similarity with candidate frequency. A histogram-matched control improves interpretation while preserving the original panels. At 0% progress, this audit remains more feasible than an unvalidated training loss or mechanistic intervention. Its potential is diagnostic: it does not establish that harder competitors are true negatives or that changing training will improve validation.",
    "implementation_notes": "Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Retain existing geometry, training-pair separation, identity, and paired perturbation diagnostics and definitions. Do not consume unavailable ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores, or simulator traits. Report unavailable category breakdowns as null with a reason.

Use view.model.eval() and torch.no_grad(), restoring the original model mode in finally. Cache at most ten batches without modifying tensors or training RNG state. Reuse the supplied family-specific sample_batch and ModelView conventions. Record batch-local row identifiers, never inferred user identifiers. Repeated histories and candidate draws remain dependent observations. Deduplicate expensive lexical retrieval by target item while applying row-specific exclusions afterward.

Obtain real-item IDs and metadata-key alignment from the host's public item mapping. Never infer real items solely from embedding-table size. If the mapping is unavailable, return an explicit unavailable result. Count training frequency exclusively from user_train['History'], counting interaction occurrences rather than unique users. Include zero-frequency real items explicitly. Use fixed bins: zero; one; two to three; four to seven; and successive powers-of-two intervals. Implement positive-frequency-bin and lexical-histogram controls using these same boundaries. Report exact frequency summaries within bins because bin matching leaves residual confounding.

Read final positions with masked physical indices, never count-1. Exclude empty histories, padding/reserved/unknown targets, and nonfinite scores with separate counts. Freeze the original final-position positive and retain original positive/negative pairs for existing diagnostics. Exclude every nonzero row-history item and the target from all competitor pools. Because loader identities are None, describe competitors as row-unobserved; do not claim exclusion against the complete user's history. A held-out positive, ownership, satisfaction, and current need cannot be inferred from these training examples.

Make lexical preprocessing fully specified and save its manifest. For each real item in ascending host integer-ID order, concatenate available title and description fields; flatten supported string lists in their stored order, apply Unicode NFKC normalization, replace whitespace runs with one space, and strip. Unsupported metadata values become missing with counts. Preserve punctuation until vectorization and use the same procedure for catalog and query items. Fit TfidfVectorizer with input='content', encoding='utf-8', decode_error='strict', strip_accents=None, lowercase=True, preprocessor=None, tokenizer=None, analyzer='word', stop_words=None, token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w+\b', ngram_range=(1,2), max_df=1.0, min_df=1, max_features=100000, vocabulary=None, binary=False, dtype=np.float32, norm='l2', use_idf=True, smooth_idf=True, sublinear_tf=False. Single-character tokens are retained deliberately because model identifiers and specifications may contain them; this also admits noise. TfidfVectorizer has no random_state parameter. Save ordered item IDs, cleaned-text hashes, fitted vocabulary and IDF, parameters, package versions, and the fitted vectorizer beneath the trial directory. Detect empty vocabulary and zero vectors; never invent matches or silently change parameters.

Keep features in CSR format. For each target, compute normalized sparse dot products against catalog blocks of at most 4096 rows, using immediate incremental top-k reduction; never allocate a catalog-square similarity matrix. Retain only strictly positive similarities after exclusions. Sort every block's eligible entries by descending similarity then ascending integer item ID before retaining its best 99; merge with the running best 99 using the same total order. This resolves boundary ties before truncation. Count all eligible positive-similarity neighbors separately from the retained neighbors. Zero vectors have zero such neighbors.

Construct four panels of exactly 99 unique competitors. Uniform: sample without replacement from all eligible real items. Positive-bin: sample without replacement from eligible items in the positive's fixed frequency bin. Lexical: use the 99 highest positive-similarity competitors. Lexical-frequency control: sample without replacement within each frequency bin to reproduce exactly the lexical panel's bin counts, then concatenate in ascending bin order. Do not exclude lexical-panel items from this control: overlap is permitted and measured; excluding them changes its sampling distribution. If a pool cannot meet its requirement, mark that panel unavailable without reducing its size or filling lexical positions with zero-similarity items. A positive-bin panel can be unavailable even when the lexical/control pair is available.

Freeze lexical panels once. Generate five draws for stochastic panels using local NumPy Generator(PCG64(SeedSequence([42, category_index, batch_index, row_index, draw_index, panel_index]))), with category order Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl and fixed panel indices. Sample from sorted eligible IDs. Persist plans, candidate IDs, identifiers, and exclusions. Reuse identical plans for any later paired model comparison; these are candidate repetitions, never additional trained models. A deterministic lexical result repeated against five controls contributes one query, not five independent queries.

Score with features B x 1 x D and candidates B x 1 x 100 through predict_score, respecting existing adapter conventions and bounded chunks. Apply the existing identity tolerances, atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4, using unchanged cloned inference. A batch identity failure invalidates its new intervention/panel comparisons and must be reported, without silently discarding failures. Require finite scores for a panel statistic and record missingness. Define positive rank as 1 plus the number of competitor scores greater than or equal to the positive score; record exact score ties separately. Record positive-minus-maximum-competitor margin, rank quantiles, and pairwise competitor intersection size and Jaccard overlap. Any top-10 inclusion statistic is explicitly a training-history panel statistic, never validation HR@10.

Report all-four-panel common-query summaries for comparability and separately labeled pair-specific summaries, especially lexical versus its frequency control, to avoid letting positive-bin eligibility hide otherwise usable contrasts. For each scope, provide row counts, nonpadding-history length, target frequency, target text length, zero-vector rate, eligible lexical-neighbor count distribution, fraction reaching 99, and excluded-query characteristics. These summaries describe sampled rows, not a user population. Average stochastic outcomes within query first; report mean paired rank differences and margin differences, plus the range and standard deviation of aggregate differences across the five draws. Call these descriptive candidate-draw variation, not confidence intervals. Without verified user identities, omit user-level bootstrap intervals. Even with identities later supplied, user uncertainty and candidate-draw variability must remain separate, and sampled-metric bias remains.

Lexical similarity to a known target is a retrospective diagnostic construction; it is unavailable for prospective recommendation and must never enter inference or a claimed deployed scoring rule. Do not interpret lexical competitors as confirmed negatives or optimize a new negative penalty from this audit alone. Training target memorization, row sampling, frequency, text availability, and lexical coverage can all produce shortcuts or selection bias. Report these limitations and keep any later training hypotheses prespecified and selected only through unchanged host macro validation HR@10. Prefix-only dropout remains an alternative, but removing prefix information may increase reliance on the final event, so its effect cannot be assumed.

No retraining or predictor modification is required for this audit. Any later training experiment preserves DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, all four routes, and the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. Exactly one independently trained HSTU checkpoint loads per category; no checkpoint averaging, independent predictors, or separately fitted score fusion. If architecture or inference changes later, update serialization and the embedded predictor writer together.",
    "pseudocode": "class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        # Retain supplied family-specific probes and their definitions.
        batches = cache_at_most_ten_batches(train_loader)
        real_ids, metadata_alignment = public_host_item_mapping_or_unavailable(self.view)
        frequencies = count_training_interactions(self.view.user_train['History'])
        bins = fixed_power_of_two_frequency_bins(frequencies, include_zero=True)
        lexical = fit_or_load_trial_local_tfidf(
            real_ids=sorted(real_ids),
            metadata=self.view.meta_data,
            alignment=metadata_alignment,
            cleaning=declared_nfkc_whitespace_rules,
            parameters=fully_declared_vectorizer_parameters)
        save_manifest_vocabulary_idf_versions_and_text_hashes(lexical)
        was_training = self.view.model.training
        self.view.model.eval()
        try:
            with torch.no_grad():
                baseline = run_retained_probes_on_cached_batches(batches)
                for batch_id, (_, seq, pos, neg) in enumerate(batches):
                    physical = torch.arange(seq.shape[1], device=seq.device)
                    end = physical[None, :].expand_as(seq).masked_fill(seq.eq(0), -1).amax(1)
                    rows = end.ge(0).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    targets = pos[rows, end[rows]]
                    rows, targets = retain_real_targets_and_record_exclusions(rows, targets, real_ids)
                    features = self.view.log2feats(seq)
                    final = features[rows, end[rows]].unsqueeze(1)
                    if not batch_identity_check(self.view, seq, rows, end,
                                                targets, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4):
                        record_invalid_batch(batch_id)
                        continue
                    for j, row_tensor in enumerate(rows):
                        row = int(row_tensor)
                        target = int(targets[j])
                        excluded = nonzero_ids(seq[row]) | {target}
                        eligible_ids = sorted(set(real_ids) - excluded)
                        positive_bin_pool = filter_bin(eligible_ids, bins[target])
                        lexical_panel, neighbor_count, lexical_reason = blocked_positive_cosine_top99(
                            lexical, target, eligible_ids,
                            catalog_block_size=4096,
                            order=('descending_similarity', 'ascending_item_id'))
                        # Block-local and merge truncations both use the full total order.
                        histogram = bin_histogram(lexical_panel) if lexical_panel is not None else None
                        record_coverage_and_excluded_query_characteristics(
                            batch_id, row, target, neighbor_count, lexical_reason,
                            positive_bin_pool, frequencies, lexical, seq[row])
                        for draw in range(5):
                            uniform = sample99_or_unavailable(
                                eligible_ids, local_rng(42, category_index, batch_id, row, draw, 0))
                            positive_bin = sample99_or_unavailable(
                                positive_bin_pool, local_rng(42, category_index, batch_id, row, draw, 1))
                            matched = sample_histogram_or_unavailable(
                                eligible_ids, bins, histogram,
                                local_rng(42, category_index, batch_id, row, draw, 3))
                            panels = {'uniform': uniform, 'positive_bin': positive_bin,
                                      'lexical': lexical_panel, 'lexical_frequency_control': matched}
                            persist_plans_and_record_panel_eligibility(panels, batch_id, row, draw)
                            for name, competitors in available_panels(panels):
                                candidates = tensor_on_device([target] + competitors).reshape(1, 1, 100)
                                scores = self.view.predict_score(final[j:j+1], candidates)
                                record_finite_statistics_or_missingness(
                                    scores, rank_rule='1 + count(competitor >= positive)',
                                    margin_rule='positive - max(competitor)',
                                    batch=batch_id, row=row, draw=draw, panel=name)
                            record_panel_intersections_and_jaccard(panels)
                metrics = summarize_all_four_common_queries_and_pair_specific_queries(
                    average_draws_within_query=True,
                    report_descriptive_draw_sd_and_range=True,
                    user_bootstrap=False,
                    retain_panel_specific_coverage=True)
                return {'metrics': merge_retained_metrics(baseline, metrics),
                        'metric_definitions': definitions_with_denominators_missingness_and_limits()}
        finally:
            self.view.model.train(was_training)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return grounded_prompt(
        measurements=raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
        definitions=raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        instructions='Use measured values and eligibility counts. Separate training-panel '
                     'stress measurements, candidate-draw variability, and pinned host validation. '
                     'Describe binned-frequency confounding, memorization, lexical coverage, '
                     'and unknown compatibility. Do not infer ownership, satisfaction, causal '
                     'preferences, true negative labels, user-level confidence intervals, '
                     'or numerical validation uplift.')",
    "originality": {
      "score": 4,
      "positive": "Combines controlled candidate composition, a lexical-frequency control, and explicit missingness within the existing HSTU diagnostic contract.",
      "negative": "Sampling controls, lexical retrieval, and repeated candidate draws are established techniques; the contribution is careful integration."
    },
    "future_potential": {
      "score": 6,
      "positive": "Can distinguish candidate-composition effects and guide prespecified single-model ablations while preserving the benchmark.",
      "negative": "Training-history panels are vulnerable to memorization and selection bias, and no supplied evidence shows that their findings predict held-out gains."
    },
    "code_difficulty": {
      "score": 5,
      "positive": "Requires no retraining, architecture changes, external data, or pretrained weights and reuses existing scoring hooks.",
      "negative": "Reproducible blocked retrieval, boundary ties, metadata alignment, matched sampling, persisted plans, and coverage-aware aggregation require more work than the original score of 3 suggested."
    }
  },
  "related_work": [
    {
      "title": "On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation",
      "link": "https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/",
      "contributions": [
        "Krichene and Rendle, KDD 2020, show that sampled recommendation metrics can reverse comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation, including in expectation.",
        "Motivates explicitly defining candidate composition and distinguishing sampling variability from sampling bias."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Repeated draws do not remove sampled-metric bias.",
        "Does not establish that these stress panels predict improvement under the pinned benchmark or justify changing its evaluator."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "Candidate Set Sampling for Evaluating Top-N Recommendation",
      "link": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11723",
      "contributions": [
        "Studies how candidate selection interacts with popularity bias.",
        "Motivates controlling candidate training-frequency distributions when comparing lexical and random competition."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The proposed lexical histogram control is an application of the methodological concern, not a validated causal identification strategy.",
        "Frequency-bin matching leaves within-bin frequency differences and other confounding."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "CATS: Cluster-Aware Thompson Sampling for Negative Mining in Sequential Recommendation",
      "link": "https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773",
      "contributions": [
        "Giulia Di Teodoro, Federico Siciliano, Nicola Tonellotto, and Fabrizio Silvestri; SIGIR 2026, pages 280–289; DOI 10.1145/3805712.3809539, as identified in the supplied verified search result.",
        "Combines item clustering with Thompson sampling and decays sampling probability from the positive item's cluster to address potential false negatives.",
        "The supplied abstract reports NDCG@10 improvements exceeding 20% over vanilla sampling and 16% over advanced sampling methods in its evaluated settings."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Reported experiments concern SASRec, BERT4Rec, BSARec and MovieLens-1M, Amazon Beauty, and BeerAdvocate; they do not establish gains for HSTU or these four categories.",
        "Clustering does not reveal a candidate's true relevance label.",
        "Does not directly validate this diagnostic design or a particular loss for uncertain competitors."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "Trading Hard Negatives and True Negatives",
      "link": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.11752",
      "contributions": [
        "IJCAI 2022 work identifies the trade-off between informative hard negatives and false negatives.",
        "Supports caution when interpreting similar unobserved items as training negatives."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not establish that lexical similarity alone identifies false negatives.",
        "Does not directly validate an HSTU training change or the proposed panel audit."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "TREC Product Recommendations: Task and Annotation Definitions",
      "link": "https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html",
      "contributions": [
        "Distinguishes substitutes, complements, compatibility judgments, and insufficient evidence.",
        "Provides vocabulary for interpreting qualitative failures while retaining unknown judgments."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Product relationships do not establish ownership, satisfaction, or current demand.",
        "Applying the taxonomy requires evidence that may be absent from available titles and descriptions."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "Scikit-learn documentation: TF–IDF, cosine similarity, chunking, and neighbor ties",
      "link": "https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html",
      "contributions": [
        "Documents vectorizer parameters, tokenization behavior, vocabulary limits, normalization, and IDF fitting; TfidfVectorizer has no random_state parameter.",
        "Cosine documentation explains sparse output and normalized dot products: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.pairwise.cosine_similarity.html.",
        "Chunking documentation supports immediate reduction: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.pairwise_distances_chunked.html.",
        "Neighbor documentation warns about equal-distance selection and input ordering: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/neighbors.html."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Sparse products can still become dense; catalog blocking and immediate reduction remain necessary.",
        "Lexical overlap is not evidence of compatibility, redundancy, current usefulness, or a true negative label.",
        "Reproducibility requires saved fitted artifacts, explicit ordering and tie handling, and pinned package versions."
      ]
    }
  ]
}
